Quick triage notes (preliminary):
- Observed spike in KV-store eviction rate aligned with p99 increase. Eviction bursts correspond to heavy reuse of a small set of prefixes.
- Result: head-of-line (HOL) blocking inside continuous-batching lanes (high-cost KV lookups blocking subsequent batches).
- Affected traffic pattern: many near-identical prompts that share long common prefixes + high concurrency from a handful of client IPs.

Telemetry snippets (excerpt):
- kv_eviction_rate: baseline ~12/min -> peaked 430/min (15:42)
- p50/p95/p99: 14ms / 78ms / 1.2s -> p99 peaked at 1.9s
- error types: transient 502s from backend timeout when the batch handler stalls

Immediate recommended mitigations (low-risk):
1) Reduce max_batch_size on OrionAI routing rule to 8 (from 32) for the next 30 minutes to prevent large batch stalls.
2) Enable per-tenant cache partitioning (soft rollout) to isolate OrionAI hot prefixes from global KV pressure.
3) Temporarily pin traffic to a slightly older model variant with smaller KV working set to reduce pressure while we dig in.

I've attached the raw eviction counters and a quick p99 graph for the window. If you can approve (1) + (2) now we can push the changes and monitor impact.

Attachments: kv_evictions_20270502.csv, p99_latency_graph.png

Summary (what happened):

Root cause (prelim): sudden KV eviction burst due to heavy reuse of long common prefixes from Orion's nightly batch workload; this generated HOL blocking in continuous-batching lanes and produced a localized throughput collapse on two nodes.

- Soft-enabled per-tenant cache partitioning to isolate hot prefixes (reduced eviction rate ~70% over 20 minutes).
- Pinned traffic for affected jobs to a lower-working-set model variant for two batch windows as a conservative fallback.
